answer: A reputation bond works like a sonnet: every agent stakes a small deposit before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers catch fake work. New identities start near the tundra of trust — almost no privileges — and must earn their way up through verified, useful tasks before reaching the zenith of full access. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones must fund each bond and spend weeks of real compute to climb, so cloning stops paying while honest agents pass for free.
